T: The last harvest is corn. Make it count.
D: Astronauts travel through a wormhole to find a new home for humanity.
P: Serve the snacks when Cooper and Donald sit on the porch with a beer.
S: Last crop corn on the cob
the farms where corn is the only crop left
Corn cobs boiled 6 minutes, brushed with butter mixed with smoked paprika and lime, charred on a hot grill and sprinkled with salt and grated parmesan.
the dust storms that roll over the farm

Fresh popcorn coated in a butter caramel with smoked paprika and sea salt, baked until glassy and crunchy, broken into clusters. Pop 100g popping corn in 2 tbsp oil and tip into a large bowl. Boil 100g butter, 150g brown sugar and 60ml golden syrup for 4 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in half a tsp bicarb soda, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1 tsp sea salt. Pour over the popcorn and toss to coat. Spread on lined trays and bake at 120C for 30 minutes, stirring twice. Cool and break into clusters.
Soft pretzel bites with beer cheese
Cooper and Donald's beers on the porch

Soft pretzel bites dipped in bicarb water, sprinkled with rock salt and baked deep brown, with a hot beer and cheddar dipping sauce. Mix 400g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt and 250ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and prove 1 hour. Roll into ropes and cut into 3cm bites. Boil 2L water with 60g bicarb soda and dip the bites for 30 seconds. Sprinkle with rock salt and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Melt 20g butter, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in 150ml lager and 100ml milk, then 200g grated cheddar and 1 tsp mustard.
M: Cooper Station chicken and corn pie
the old farmhouse, rebuilt in orbit

Chicken thighs poached, shredded and folded into a creamy sauce with corn, leek and thyme, topped with shortcrust pastry and baked at 200C for 30 minutes until golden. Poach 800g chicken thighs and shred. Soften a sliced leek in butter, add 2 tbsp flour, 200ml stock and 200ml cream, then the chicken, 200g corn kernels and thyme. Tip into a dish, top with 2 sheets shortcrust and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

Pork shoulder rubbed with garlic, rosemary and salt, roasted slow until tender, the crackling blasted until it shatters, with roast potatoes and apple sauce. Score the skin of a 2kg pork shoulder, rub with salt and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Make cuts in the flesh and push in 4 garlic slivers and rosemary. Roast at 160C for 4 hours. Turn up to 240C for 25 minutes until the crackling blisters. Roast 1kg potatoes in oil alongside for the last hour. Simmer 3 chopped apples with 2 tbsp sugar and water and mash for apple sauce.
W: A sweet, custardy buttermilk pie with vanilla and fresh nutmeg in a crisp shortcrust case, served cool with lightly whipped cream and berries. Blind bake a 23cm sweet shortcrust case at 180C for 15 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 250g caster sugar, 60g melted butter, 2 tbsp plain flour, 250ml buttermilk, 1 tsp vanilla and a good grating of nutmeg until smooth. Pour into the case and bake at 170C for 45 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool completely. Serve with whipped cream and fresh berries.
K: the beer on the porch at dusk

Cold lager topped with homemade lemonade of fresh lemon juice and sugar syrup, poured into frosted glasses with a lemon wheel. Frost four glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Dissolve 80g sugar in 80ml hot water and cool. Squeeze 4 lemons and mix the juice with the syrup and 300ml cold soda water. Half fill each glass with cold lager, about 190ml, then top with the lemonade. Add a lemon wheel and serve on the porch.
